shield at a2 AND wall between b1|b2 → LOS BLOCKED at corner (0.5,0.5) [CRR p.28]

shield on b1 only (1 obstacle at corner 0.5,0.5) → LOS allowed

atoms.summary: Figures perform attacks to defeat hostile figures; each attack uses an attack type (Melee/Ranged), attack dice, and surge abilities sourced from the weapon Item card (hero) or Deployment card (non-hero).

atoms.notes: Hero weapon-Item-card interaction is a campaign subsystem. The skirmish bot does not model hero weapon items as separate attachable cards, so this rule has no in-engine surface to pin.

atoms.summary: When a DC figure performs an attack using an alternate attack pool, they may still trigger their own surge abilities unless the triggering ability states otherwise.

assertions: 004a: source — getAttackerSurgeAbilities reads surges keyed on attacker DC (not on dice pool)
004b: source — the ONLY full opt-out is combat.blockSurgeAbilities (no dice-pool predicate)
004c: source — the final surge list is base + doubles + bonus (all attacker-DC-derived)
004d: source — pendingOverrideAttackDice mutates attackInfo only (not the surge set)
004e: source — explicit opt-out path exists (Tusken Cycler wires blockSurgeAbilities via _pendingBlockSurgeAbilities)

atoms.notes: Surge-ability gathering is decoupled from the dice pool by construction: getAttackerSurgeAbilities keys on attackerDcName (or defenderDcName under Reverse Engineer), never on attackInfo.dice or pendingOverrideAttackDice. The sole full opt-out is an explicit blockSurgeAbilities flag (e.g. Tusken Cycler) wired via overrideDice.blockSurgeAbilities, matching the CRR's 'unless the triggering ability states otherwise' carve-out.

assertions: 018a: source — the attack pool is a single `let dice = [...baseDice];` accumulator

atoms.summary: Some missions specify that certain doors are locked; locked doors cannot be opened except as specified in the mission rules; a locked door can have Health and when destroyed it is removed from the map; mission rules may specify how to unlock.
atoms.notes: Locked-door mission mechanic is campaign-specific. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Some missions allow heroes to place doors; doors must be placed on exactly two edges and cannot overlap a wall or another door.
atoms.notes: Hero door placement is a campaign-only mission mechanic. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Crate tokens do not block line of sight or figure movement; figures may move through and end their movement in the same space as a crate token.

assertions: PROBE-PD-CRT-001: Crate tokens do not block LOS
crate tokens must not block LOS

atoms.summary: If a crate token is in a space containing terrain, the terrain in the space still takes effect (e.g., blocking terrain with a crate still blocks).
atoms.implementationArea: src/game/movement.js (terrain keyed by coord, not by token overlay)

assertions: 002a: source — movement.js does not read cratePositions (terrain is independent)
002b: behavior — a difficult cell with a crate overlay still costs +1
002c: terrain is stored in mapSpaces.terrain, not in any token map

atoms.summary: During a campaign, crates are objects that heroes can interact with to Claim the token and draw a Supply card.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only Claim + Supply card mechanic. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: During a campaign, at the end of each mission, heroes receive 50 credits for each crate token they have in their play areas.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only credit reward. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: The color of crate tokens has no game effect unless specified by the mission.
atoms.notes: Mission-token color-neutrality is a mission-scope definitional rule. Skirmish has no engine surface that inspects crate colors.

atoms.summary: A crate token with its colored side down cannot be examined by players; this color is hidden information.
atoms.notes: Campaign hidden-information mechanic. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Terminal tokens are placed on the map as indicated by the mission's diagram.
atoms.notes: Definitional placement; functional terminal effect is pinned at CRR-TRM-002 (skirmish CC bonus).

atoms.summary: In a skirmish, each player draws one additional Command card during the Status Phase for each terminal the player controls.

assertions: 004b: terminal bonus = +1 per terminal controlled
004f: terminal + RHC stacking is additive

atoms.summary: Terminals do not block line of sight or movement; figures can end their movement in the same space as a terminal token.

assertions: PROBE-PD-TRM-003: Terminal tokens do not block LOS
terminal tokens must not block LOS

atoms.summary: If a terminal is in a space containing terrain, the terrain in the space still takes effect (e.g., blocking terrain with a terminal still blocks).
atoms.implementationArea: src/game/movement.js (terrain keyed by coord, not by token overlay)

assertions: 004a: source — movement.js does not read terminal-position maps (terrain is independent)
004b: behavior — a difficult cell retains +1 surcharge regardless of token overlay

atoms.summary: The colors of terminal tokens have no game effect unless specified by the mission.
atoms.notes: Mission-token color-neutrality is mission-scope definitional. Skirmish has no engine surface that inspects terminal colors.

atoms.summary: A terminal token with its colored side down cannot be examined by players; this color is hidden information.
atoms.notes: Campaign hidden-information mechanic. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Walls are solid black lines along map-tile boundaries; figures cannot move or trace line of sight through walls.

assertions: PROBE-WASS-002: activates only when both endpoints are difficult
shield at a2 AND wall between b1|b2 → LOS BLOCKED at corner (0.5,0.5) [CRR p.28]

atoms.summary: Walls are not terrain and are not affected by abilities that affect terrain — Massive figures can enter blocking terrain but cannot move through walls.
atoms.notes: Composite rule: (a) walls are not terrain — structurally true in the data model (walls live in impassableEdges, terrain in the terrain map, separate concepts/shapes), (b) Massive figures enter blocking terrain (CRR-MSV-003) but (c) no figure — including Massive — may cross walls (CRR-MOVE-010 / CRR-WAL-001). The conjunction is the pinned invariants composed.

atoms.summary: Walls only block line of sight along an entire edge of a space; if a wall does not cover an entire edge, line of sight may be traced to, from, and through that edge or corner.
atoms.notes: Partial-edge-wall LOS behavior is exercised by the diagonal-corner carveout probes (CRR-ES-003) where walls interact with the 0.5,0.5 corner geometry.

atoms.summary: Mission tokens represent objects, people, or points of interest; they have no inherent effects and act as specified in the mission.
atoms.notes: Mission-token-as-mission-specific-effect is definitional; no engine pin names mission tokens generically. Phase-D gap.

atoms.summary: Three types of mission tokens: Rebel, Imperial, and neutral (distinguished by icon).
atoms.notes: Token-type enumeration is mission-data definitional. Skirmish scope excludes (per-mission handling).

atoms.summary: Mission tokens do not block line of sight or affect figure movement; figures can enter and end their movement in the same space as a mission token.
atoms.notes: Mission tokens are objects (per CRR-MSN-001); OBJ-002 pins the 'non-door objects are transparent to LOS and do not block movement' rule for all object subtypes.

atoms.summary: If a mission token is in a space containing terrain, the terrain in the space still takes effect.
atoms.notes: General MISSION-TOKEN restatement of the token-on-terrain precedence rule. Already pinned for the two concrete mission-token subtypes (crate, terminal) — the invariant holds because terrain is keyed by coord in src/game/movement.js and is not overlaid by any token kind.

atoms.summary: The colored border of mission tokens has no game effect unless specified by the mission; a neutral mission token with colored side down cannot be examined (color is hidden information).
atoms.notes: Color-neutrality + hidden-information rule is mission-specific / campaign-only. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: In a campaign, green deployment points are active at the start of each mission; other deployment points are not active until specified by the mission's rules.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only mechanic. Skirmish uses deployment zones (CRR-DEPL-001), not deployment points. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Entrance refers to the space containing the entrance token; heroes are deployed to the entrance token at the start of a mission in a campaign.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only hero deployment mechanic. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: During a campaign, some effects instruct figures to perform attribute tests; the player rolls the dice listed below that attribute icon and succeeds on rolling at least one success icon.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only attribute test mechanic. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Each game effect requiring an attribute test specifies the pass/fail outcome; many attribute tests require a figure to interact with an object (attribute tests on objects).
atoms.notes: Campaign-only mission mechanic. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Multi-success attribute tests place strain tokens on the object for each success rolled; the next figure discards those tokens for +1 per token on their next attempt.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only multi-success attribute-test save mechanic. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Only heroes roll dice for attribute tests; elite figures automatically receive 1 success; regular figures automatically fail.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only attribute-test figure-type rule. See CRR-ELI-004 for the elite-auto-success cross-reference. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Conditions are ongoing effects applied to figures; each condition has an ability that applies to the figure as long as it has that condition.
atoms.notes: Umbrella definition — per-condition atoms (BLED, FOC, HID, STN, WKN) collectively exercise the "ongoing effect while condition held" shape. No single oracle pins the umbrella wording.

atoms.summary: When a hero gains a condition, the corresponding Condition card is placed next to the hero; for other figures a condition token is placed next to the figure. The token stays with the figure if it moves or is placed in another space.
atoms.notes: Hero-card-vs-token presentation distinction is campaign-only (skirmish has no heroes). Skirmish always uses the figure-keyed figureConditions map (no physical token placement). Exempt for skirmish scope; the movement-persistence consequence is pinned by CRR-CND-003.

atoms.summary: A condition on a figure stays with that figure when it moves or is placed in another space.
atoms.notes: Storage shape pinned by PROBE-COND-008 (game.figureConditions is keyed by figureKey, a string that is stable across moves/places; see tests/domain/oracle/multi-condition-probes.test.js 'pins the array-of-strings storage shape' and 'applyCondition appends to per-figure array — the storage shape that enables independence'). No oracle pins a move-then-assert-condition-present sequence directly; the storage invariant plus the fact that movement.js/place code does not mutate figureConditions structurally guarantees this. Phase-D may add a direct probe later.

atoms.summary: Each Condition card lists when the condition is discarded; when that situation occurs, the card/token is discarded and the figure no longer follows the rules.
atoms.notes: Umbrella discard-trigger rule. Per-condition discard triggers are pinned by FOC-002 (after attack/test), HID-002 (after attack), STN-003 (action), WKN-002 (end-of-activation), BLED-001 (surge-to-discard). No single assertion pins the umbrella.

atoms.summary: Conditions have the BENEFICIAL or HARMFUL trait. Focused and Hidden are BENEFICIAL; Bleeding, Stunned, and Weakened are HARMFUL. The trait has no inherent effect but may be referenced by abilities.

assertions: HARMFUL_CONDITIONS = ['Stun', 'Bleed', 'Weaken']
each harmful condition in HARMFUL_CONDITIONS can coexist with every other

atoms.notes: HARMFUL set explicitly enumerated; BENEFICIAL set is the complement (Focus, Hide). Engine stores both sets as condition-name strings ('Focus', 'Hide', 'Stun', 'Bleed', 'Weaken').

atoms.summary: A figure cannot be affected by multiple instances of the same condition; attempting to apply an already-present condition has no effect.

assertions: PROBE-COND-002: dedup — applyCondition twice is a no-op on state
second apply returns false; array length unchanged; no duplicate stored
applyCondition dedups by name (returns false) — independence precondition

atoms.summary: Attacks with a condition keyword (Focus, Hide, Bleed, Stun, Weaken) apply the corresponding condition only if the target suffers ≥1 damage in step 7; the condition is applied after the attack resolves.

assertions: 001b: zero damage blocks Bleed application
002b: positive damage applies Bleed
Surge conditions (Stun, Bleed, Weaken) apply ONLY when final damage > 0

atoms.notes: Positive/negative probes pinned via Bleed as the representative harmful condition; the handler path is shared for all surge-condition keywords (see combat.js damage gate).

atoms.summary: BENEFICIAL conditions from a keyword attack are applied to the attacker; HARMFUL conditions are applied to the target.
atoms.notes: Per-condition oracles pin the direction: Focus (BENEFICIAL) lands on attacker via condition-dice-oracles.test.js 'adds green die when Focus is newly applied'; Bleed/Stun/Weaken (HARMFUL) land on target via combat-handler-oracles '002b: positive damage applies Bleed'. No single assertion pins the direction-rule umbrella wording.

atoms.summary: Objects cannot gain conditions.
atoms.notes: Architectural invariant: applyCondition(game, figureKey, cond) writes into game.figureConditions[figureKey]. Objects (crates/terminals) live in separate maps (cratePositions, crateHealth, crateTokens, deviceTokens) with no condition-storage field. No code path maps an object identifier into figureConditions.

assertions: 009a: applyCondition signature pins its parameter as figureKey
009b: no object-level condition storage exists (no crateConditions / terminalConditions fields)
009d: applying a condition only mutates figureConditions (round-trip)

atoms.summary: During a campaign a hero is healthy as long as not wounded; other figures are healthy until defeated.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only hero Healthy/Wounded state machine (gated by 'During a campaign' in CRR). Skirmish uses only the defeated/not-defeated distinction already exercised by the DEFEATED section. Exempt for skirmish scope.

atoms.summary: During a figure's activation, it may perform two actions; available actions are Attack, Move, Interact, Rest (only heroes can rest); figures may have one or more Special actions.
atoms.notes: Umbrella definition of the four action types. Rest is hero/campaign-only and out of skirmish scope. Behavioral consequences are pinned by ACT-006, ACV-002, ATK-029.

atoms.summary: A figure is not required to perform both actions during its activation.
atoms.notes: Definitional (no-action-required) consequence. Exercised implicitly by the End-Activation button which is available at any point during a figure's activation (see ACV-005).

atoms.summary: Each action must be resolved completely before the figure performs its next action.
atoms.notes: No named assertion pins the 'resolve one action completely before starting another' invariant. Engine enforces via dcActionsData transitions but not by a direct oracle. Phase-D gap.

atoms.summary: Special actions are denoted by ♦; a single ♦ costs one action, two ♦ icons cost two actions but are treated as one ability; special actions containing multiple attacks or a move+attack still cost only the listed number of actions.

assertions: 004a: CC specials tag actionCost: 1
004b: CC doubles tag actionCost: 2
004c: DC specials read per-index cost from specialCosts (default 1)
004d: insufficient-action gate rejects specials that cost more than remaining
004e: action deduction uses _effectiveActionCost for dc_special_, else 1
004f: reducer DcActionPerformed subtracts payload.actionCost (default 1)

atoms.summary: Movement points may be spent before or after performing an action; MP gained as part of a special action must be spent during that action.
atoms.notes: Movement-bank interleaving with actions is exercised by movement-pick-behavioral but no named assertion pins the 'MP from special action must be spent during that action' restriction. Phase-D gap.

atoms.summary: A figure can perform the same action multiple times per activation except: a non-hero figure can only use one of its actions to attack per activation (including special actions that contain attacks).
atoms.notes: Non-hero one-attack-per-activation is pinned by ATK-029 (move-features.test.js 'already attacked this activation → 0'). The broader 'same action repeatable' rule has no direct pin but follows from the action-loop design; treat as covered via ATK-029 anchor.

atoms.summary: A figure can perform each special action (♦) only once per activation.

assertions: rejects duplicate special (specialsUsed)
already been used

atoms.summary: In the Legends of the Alliance companion app, actions presented with the action-arrow icon are not considered special actions and are not limited to once per activation.
atoms.notes: Explicitly companion-app / campaign-scoped. Skirmish-only scope excludes this.

atoms.summary: Numerous game effects allow figures to perform an attack, rest, interact, or move without performing an action.
atoms.notes: Free-attack-outside-activation is the canonical case; pinned by ATK-030 (free-attack-surfacing-probes 001a/001b). Free moves/interacts follow the same flag-driven pattern.

atoms.summary: During each Activation Phase, each figure receives one activation; during a figure's activation, it performs up to two actions.
atoms.notes: Umbrella statement. Per-figure activation semantics and 2-action limit are pinned behaviorally by ACV-002 (alternation), ACT-006 (action-type restrictions), and ACT-001 (action types).

atoms.summary: Players alternate resolving activations; when resolving an activation, a player chooses one ready friendly group to activate; after a player finishes an activation, the opponent resolves an activation.

assertions: 002: consumes pendingEndTurn and flips turn to opponent
003: three-step dance completes — pendingEndTurn flows through, turn switches

atoms.notes: Alternation is the load-bearing invariant; activation-sequencing 002 pins the turn-flip on End-Turn press. Ready-group selection is a separate UI layer not pinned by this atom.

atoms.summary: While activating a group of two or more figures, the player activates all figures in the order of their choice; both actions must be resolved for each figure before the next figure activates, and before the opponent resolves an activation.
atoms.notes: Intra-group figure-order and 'both-actions-before-next-figure' sequencing is enforced by the DG iteration in activation-setup.js but no named assertion pins the ordering invariant. Phase-D gap.

atoms.summary: Campaign-only activation rules: Rebels first; heroes may strain for MP; hero activation tokens in low-hero games; heroes ready cards at start of activation; Rebel choice of second-activation-token holder.
atoms.notes: Entire bullet block explicitly gated by 'During a campaign'. Skirmish-only scope excludes this.

atoms.summary: After performing up to two actions and 'during your activation' abilities, a figure declares the end of its activation; the player may end early; remaining actions and unspent movement points do not carry over to the figure's next activation.

assertions: 005a: source — movementBank is listed as a per-activation per-msgId flag
005b: source — cleanupActivation deletes every per-msgId flag for the ending msgId
005d: behavior — cleanupActivation empties the msgId movementBank entry
005e: behavior — next activation starts with no inherited MP

atoms.summary: After resolving a group's activation, exhaust the hero's activation token (for heroes) or Deployment card (for all other groups); after activating a Companion, exhaust the Companion card.
atoms.notes: DC-exhaust-after-activation is the canonical EXHAUST semantics pinned by the EXHAUST section atoms. Companion-exhaust-after-activation is a special case that follows the same flag-bit pattern.

atoms.summary: If all friendly groups are exhausted, that player cannot perform an activation; the player's opponent continues to resolve activations until all groups are exhausted.

assertions: 003c: player has 0 activations, opponent still has some → forced pass

atoms.summary: Abilities that can be used during a figure's activation are used before or after either of that figure's two actions, not while performing actions or other abilities.
atoms.notes: 'Inter-action ability window' is engine-enforced by the dcActionsData finite state machine but not pinned by a dedicated oracle. Phase-D gap.

atoms.summary: The first phase of each round is the Activation Phase; during this phase players alternate activating groups of figures until all groups are exhausted.
atoms.notes: Phase ordering is pinned structurally by round-lifecycle-behavioral 013a-013e (START_OF_ROUND → ACTIVATION → END_OF_ROUND). Activation alternation behavior is pinned by ACV-002.

atoms.summary: While activating a group of two or more figures, the player activates all figures one at a time in the order of their choice.
atoms.notes: Duplicated by ACV-003 within the ACTIVATION section. Same engine invariant; same Phase-D gap disposition.

atoms.summary: During a campaign mission, Rebel and Imperial players alternate activating groups; the Rebel players resolve the first activation each round.
atoms.notes: Explicitly campaign-scoped. Skirmish-only scope excludes this.

atoms.summary: During a skirmish, players alternate activating groups, starting with the player with initiative each round.

assertions: 004a: source — Activation Phase opens with currentActivationTurnPlayerId set to initiativePlayerId (round.js)
004c: source — after an activation ends, the turn flips to the other player (alternation pin)
004d: source — pass action also flips turn to the other player (alternation pin)
004f: source — initiative passes each round; next round opens with the new initiative player

atoms.summary: In Four-Player Skirmishes, each player in clockwise order activates one of their ready groups.
atoms.notes: Four-Player Team Battle is explicitly out of the skirmish-bot scope (_meta.scope=skirmish, 2-player).

atoms.summary: During a skirmish, if a player has fewer ready Deployment cards than any of their opponents, that player may choose not to activate a group and pass play back to their opponent.

assertions: handlePassActivationTurn must be the exported pass handler — CRR-APH-006
pass handler must read the current player activations remaining — CRR-APH-006
pass handler must read the opponent activations remaining — CRR-APH-006
pass must be rejected when otherRem <= myRem — CRR-APH-006
legal pass must flip turn to otherPlayerId — CRR-APH-006
pass button must render only when current player is strictly behind — CRR-APH-006

atoms.summary: Numerous abilities, mission rules, and other game effects can be triggered at the same time.
atoms.notes: Umbrella framing. Behavioral consequences are pinned by CNF-002..CNF-008.

atoms.summary: While attacking, mission rules and effects from conditions are resolved with priority, followed by effects from the attacker (including friendly figures), then effects from the defender (including friendly figures).
atoms.notes: Combat step ordering within a single attack IS enforced (combat-timing-behavioral, combat-reactions-behavioral) but no named assertion pins the precise 'mission+conditions first, then attacker, then defender' priority order when multiple optional effects compete in a single step. Phase-D gap.

atoms.summary: While attacking during a Four-Player Team Battle, priority order extends to attacker's teammate then defender's teammate after attacker/defender.
atoms.notes: Four-Player Team Battle is out of scope (skirmish-bot is 2-player).

atoms.summary: Effects from multiple figures under the control of a single player are resolved in the order of that player's choice.
atoms.notes: Player-choice ordering for multi-figure simultaneous effects (e.g., multiple reaction prompts) is implemented as sequential prompts but no named assertion pins the 'resolver chooses order' rule. Phase-D gap.

atoms.summary: The decision for a player to resolve an optional ability coincides with the order of resolution; after a player has declined to trigger one or more abilities, the player does not have the opportunity to trigger that ability until the next triggering instance.

assertions: skip path clears pendingToughLuck without mutating dice
TL clears pendingToughLuck on both remove and skip

atoms.summary: Campaign conflict resolution: outside attacks — mission rules first, then Imperial player effects, then Rebel player effects; Imperial decides mission-rule tie order; Rebels collectively decide their tie order; Imperial breaks hero decision deadlocks.
atoms.notes: Explicitly campaign-scoped (CONFLICTS IN A CAMPAIGN subsection).

atoms.summary: Skirmish outside of attacks: mission rules are resolved first, followed by effects from the player with initiative, then effects from each other player proceeding clockwise.

assertions: 004a: P1 has initiative → P1 Brush logs before P2 Brush
004b: P2 has initiative → P2 Brush logs before P1 Brush

atoms.notes: Start-of-Round 'Brush' effect fires per-DC; 004a/004b pin the initiative-first ordering of player effects outside attacks. Mission-rules-first half is not directly probed but follows from runStartOfRoundDcEffects resolving mission-scoped pending before player-owned DC effects.

atoms.summary: If multiple mission rules would resolve at the same time, the player with initiative decides their order.
atoms.notes: Initiative breaks multi-mission-rule ties. No named assertion pins this tiebreak semantics at the mission-rule level (as opposed to the per-DC Brush-style effects pinned by CNF-007). Phase-D gap.

atoms.summary: During a skirmish, one player has the initiative token each game round; the player with initiative resolves the first activation during that game round.
atoms.notes: Initiative-first ordering for start-of-round / outside-attack effects is pinned by CNF-007 (sor-sequencing 004a/004b). The 'first activation of the round' half is adjacent behavior in the same ordering system (ACV-002 alternation + initiative-first entry).

atoms.summary: At mission start, the player with the lowest total cost of Deployment cards chooses which player begins with the initiative token; ties are decided randomly; the initiative player also chooses deployment zones and resolves the first activation during round 1.
atoms.notes: Pre-game setup rule. The skirmish-bot treats initiative as an assigned game-state attribute at game-start; the setup choice procedure is outside the live engine scope.

atoms.summary: The player with initiative breaks all ties for mission rules (e.g., if a mission rule moves a token toward the closest figure and multiple figures are equidistant, initiative chooses).
atoms.notes: Initiative-breaks-all-ties-for-mission-rules has no named assertion pin. Mission-rule tiebreaks (e.g., closest-figure disambiguation) are currently engine-deterministic via stable iteration order; conformance to 'initiative player chooses' is not audited. Phase-D gap (potential future divergence).

atoms.summary: For a single-figure group, the figure cost is equal to the group's deployment cost.

assertions: attacker gains kill VP equal to deployment cost

atoms.summary: For a multi-figure group, the figure cost is equal to the figure's reinforcement cost.

assertions: should be only reinforcement cost, not including attachment VP
no attachment VP awarded for non-last figure

atoms.notes: Multi-figure group: per-figure VP awarded on each defeat equals the deployment cards reinforcement (sub)cost, not the full group deployment cost. Stormtrooper (Regular) defeat probe asserts vpGained is less than full-group cost + attachment.

atoms.summary: A companion has a figure cost of 0.

assertions: companions cost 0 (explicit or undefined = 0)

atoms.notes: Companion dc-effects entries have cost=0 (or undefined defaulting to 0). Oracle iterates The Child, Salacious B. Crumb, Dio, J4X-7, Junk Droid, BD-1 and asserts cost === 0 || undefined.

atoms.summary: Other figures (e.g., captive from 'Imperial Hospitality') have a figure cost of 0.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only mission-introduced figures (captives, neutral mission figures). Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: All figures belonging to a player are friendly toward one another.
atoms.notes: Structural invariant: figures are owned by playerNum; same-owner = friendly is tautological in the engine data model. No separate 'friendliness' check exists (or is needed) because friendly-targetable effects iterate game.figurePositions[ownerPn].

atoms.summary: A figure is friendly to itself.
atoms.notes: Definitional self-friendliness. Engine iterates own-owner figure positions including self; self-inclusion is the default for friendly-iteration helpers (Fury of Kashyyyk, Shared Intuition, Spectre Cell, etc.).

atoms.summary: During a campaign, all Rebel figures are friendly toward one another; all Imperial and Mercenary figures are friendly toward one another.
atoms.notes: Campaign affiliation friendliness. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Regular/Four-Player Free-For-All skirmish: all other players are opponents, their figures are hostile. Four-Player Team Battle: immediate neighbors are opponents, remaining player is teammate.
atoms.notes: Two-player skirmish friendliness is identity (playerNum match); four-player variants are out of scope. The two-player mapping is structurally enforced via opponentPlayerNum() helper in src/game/player-helpers.js.

atoms.summary: Players cannot target friendly figures with attacks.
atoms.notes: Same rule as CRR-ATK-009; see PROBE-PD-ATK-009 in phase-d-target-invariants.test.js.

atoms.summary: All figures belonging to a player's opponent are considered hostile.
atoms.notes: Structural: figure owner != viewer = hostile. Derived from player-number comparison, no separate hostility attribute. opponentPlayerNum() in src/game/player-helpers.js implements the inverse.

atoms.summary: During a campaign, all Imperial figures are considered hostile to all Rebel and Mercenary figures.
atoms.notes: Campaign affiliation hostility. Skirmish scope excludes.

atoms.summary: Regular/Four-Player Free-For-All and Four-Player Team Battle skirmish hostility rules (identical in shape to FRIENDLY FIGURE rules).
atoms.notes: Duplicates FRF-004 inverse. Two-player hostility = !own-owner, structurally encoded. Four-player variants out of scope.

atoms.summary: During a campaign, each Rebel player controls a hero; 'Hero' refers to hero figures, the controlling player, and associated components. Some heroes use unique tokens (Saska-Device, Loku-Recon, Tress-Style).
atoms.notes: Campaign-only. Skirmish treats heroes (when present as skirmish DCs) as ordinary figures with their DC stats; hero-player / hero-sheet semantics do not apply in skirmish.

atoms.summary: A figure can perform an interact as an action.

assertions: 003: Bossk (normal) at terminal h21 → interact offered

atoms.summary: A figure must be in the same space as or adjacent to an object in order to interact with it.

assertions: 003: Bossk (normal) at terminal h21 → interact offered
001: Nexu (Non-Sentient) at terminal h21 → no interact offered

atoms.notes: PROBE-INT-003 proves adjacency-at-terminal-surfaces-interact; PROBE-INT-001 proves the inverse surface (though filter reason differs, same adjacency precondition).

atoms.summary: During a campaign, a hero can interact with a crate token to claim the token and draw one Supply card.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only crate-claim + Supply-draw. Skirmish crate interaction is covered separately by CRATE TOKENS atoms (CRT section).

atoms.summary: Mission rules will often list different tasks that can be performed by interacting, such as using terminals or retrieving tokens.
atoms.notes: Mission-rule interact tasks are section-specific (TERMINAL TOKENS, CRATE TOKENS, MISSION TOKENS); already covered by those seeded sections and their mission-scoring probes.

atoms.summary: If mission rules have an attribute icon in parentheses after the target of an interact, the figure must pass the corresponding attribute test to resolve the effect.
atoms.notes: Attribute-gated interact (e.g., (Tech) or (Insight) in mission rules) is implemented per-mission in skirmish missions that use it, but no general oracle asserts 'interact resolves only on passed attribute test'. Per-mission attribute-test gates (ATT section) are covered; the interact-gate binding is not explicitly pinned. Phase-D gap.

atoms.summary: Interact references doors (open via interact), crates, terminals, retrieving tokens, and Supply cards as interactable objects.
atoms.notes: Related-topics aggregator. Each object-interact surface is covered by its object section (DOORS, CRATE TOKENS, TERMINAL TOKENS).

atoms.summary: Deployment cards with a Neutral icon and card back do not belong to any affiliation; during skirmish army-building, a player may include them as if they belonged to their affiliation.
atoms.notes: Pre-game army-building rule. Skirmish-bot accepts arbitrary DCs provided they exist in DC data; no runtime affiliation-gate for Neutral DCs is required or enforced.

atoms.summary: Neutral Deployment cards cannot be used in a campaign.

atoms.summary: When a figure is incapacitated, it discards all conditions, and conditions cannot be applied to that figure.
atoms.notes: Condition-discard on incapacitation. Not exercised by current missions.

atoms.summary: An incapacitated figure cannot suffer damage or be targeted/affected by attacks, abilities, or game effects (except as specified by mission rules); its abilities are not available.
atoms.notes: Targeting and damage immunity for incapacitated figures. Not exercised by current skirmish missions.

atoms.summary: An incapacitated figure can still be pushed by a massive figure ending its movement in the incapacitated figure's space.
atoms.notes: Massive-push exception for incapacitated figures. Not exercised by current skirmish missions.

atoms.summary: Interrupt abilities pause the current action/ability, fully resolve, and then the paused action/ability resumes from the interruption point.

assertions: figure survives interrupt damage and remains in figurePositions

atoms.notes: Interrupt pause/resume contract pinned by interrupt-predefeat-behavioral (survivor case: figure absorbs interrupt damage mid-attack and attack resumes).

atoms.summary: If an interrupt makes the current action/ability invalid, that effect is not resolved, but any costs used to resolve that effect are still paid.
atoms.notes: Cost-is-paid-even-if-invalidated rule. Exercised inline by e.g., Assassinate interrupts; no isolated oracle pinning the "cost paid even on invalidation" invariant.

atoms.summary: A figure's action cannot be interrupted while the figure is in a space containing another figure.
atoms.notes: Same-space-no-interrupt rule (protects resolving figures from interrupt loopholes when co-located with large figures). Niche; no oracle.

atoms.summary: Attribute tests and attacks can gain negative versions of symbols. A positive and a negative version of the same symbol eliminate each other immediately; a negative symbol has no other effect.

assertions: 003a: defender weakened — reduces effective block after pierce
003b: attacker weakened — reduces damage after block subtraction
003c: attacker weakened can reduce damage to 0
003e: both weakened — defender weaken then attacker weaken in sequence

atoms.notes: Weakened is the canonical negative-symbol source (-1 attack / -1 block). Combat-oracles 003a/b/c/e pin positive/negative cancellation semantics across attacker and defender.

atoms.summary: Weakened (-1 attack / -1 defense) is a canonical source of negative symbols in attack/defense results.
atoms.notes: Weakened semantics fully defined in WKN atoms; this entry is a pointer.

atoms.summary: In a Skirmish, when an ability instructs a player to pay another player VPs, the paying player loses VPs and the paid player gains an equal number of VPs.

assertions: 001a: behavior — deductVp(N) + awardObjectiveVp(N) preserves total VP across both players
001b: behavior — payment amount is the same number on both sides (no asymmetry)
001c: source — Hondo Negotiate pays 2 VP via symmetric pair (deductVp + awardObjectiveVp)
001d: recipient gain goes to objectives (not kills); paid VP is objective VP

atoms.summary: If an ability requires a player to pay more VPs than they have, that player cannot use the ability; if it requires an opponent to pay more than they have, the opponent pays all of their remaining VPs.
atoms.notes: Self-pay-insufficient branch pinned by VPS-004; opponent-pay-all branch is a gap in that atom's corollary.

atoms.summary: When a figure with a power token declares an attack or is declared as target, it may spend 1 of its power tokens to apply +1 of that token's symbol to the attack/defense results.

assertions: attacker spending Damage token adds +1 bonusHits
defender spending Block token adds +1 bonusBlock and sets tracking flags
attacker spending Surge token adds +1 tokenSurgeBonus
defender spending Evade token adds +1 bonusEvade

atoms.notes: Power-token spend handler is handleCombatToken in src/handlers/combat.js — Damage/Surge bonuses for attacker, Block/Evade bonuses for defender. Tests B-C-TOKEN-001 through B-C-TOKEN-004 pin each symbol application path.

atoms.summary: A figure can only spend a power token of the appropriate type: the attacker cannot spend block/evade tokens; the defender cannot spend damage/surge tokens.

assertions: getEligibleTokens must use role-gated allowed set — CRR-PT-002
getEligibleTokens must filter by allowed.includes(type) — CRR-PT-002
Squad Cohesion must reject donor tokens of the wrong type — CRR-PT-002
attacker eligibility must include Damage/Surge/Wild, exclude Block/Evade — CRR-PT-002
defender eligibility must include Block/Evade/Wild, exclude Damage/Surge — CRR-PT-002

atoms.summary: Each figure can have at most 2 total power tokens; excess on grant forces discard down to 2.

assertions: game-helpers.js always pushes tokens before checking overflow
game-helpers.js queues pendingPowerTokenOverflow on overflow
Shield grant to figure already at cap queues overflow instead of refusing
Hold the Line granting 3 Block to figure at cap-1 overflows by 2
selfPlay mode discards oldest tokens to stay at cap

atoms.notes: Cap=2 + overflow queue pinned by power-token-grant-oracles. selfPlay branch directly exercises the forced-discard path.

atoms.summary: When an ability refers to the wild power token, the player can choose any power token type.

assertions: sendWildTypeWindow must scope Wild options to the role-native pair — CRR-PT-004
Wild option buttons must emit the combat_token_<gid>_wild_<type> customId — CRR-PT-004
combat_token router must accept att|def|wild role segments — CRR-PT-004
attacker Wild must resolve to Damage/Surge — CRR-PT-004
defender Wild must resolve to Block/Evade — CRR-PT-004

atoms.summary: A figure cannot spend more than 1 power token per attack.
atoms.implementationArea: src/handlers/combat.js (advanceTokenPhase, handleCombatToken, sendTokenWindow linear state machine)

assertions: 005a: source — advanceTokenPhase clears tokenPhase on entry and only promotes attacker → defender
005b: source — there is exactly one promotion to defender inside advanceTokenPhase (no loop-back to attacker)
005c: source — handleCombatToken guards on tokenPhase match (second click after spend is rejected because tokenPhase is null)
005d: source — each of the three spend branches (direct / squad-cohesion / wild) ends with exactly one advanceTokenPhase call
005e: source — sendTokenWindow is opened at most once per attack per role; every opener first sets tokenPhase to match
005f: source — after a spend, the spent token is removed from the figure pool (one-way consumption)

atoms.notes: Token phase is a strict linear state machine: attacker (optional, one-shot) → defender (optional, one-shot) → proceedAfterTokens. advanceTokenPhase clears tokenPhase then promotes at most once; handleCombatToken's `if (combat.tokenPhase !== expectedPhase) return` guard blocks a second click after any spend.

atoms.summary: When a rule or ability instructs a player to reveal a card, the player shows it to all players, and after the ability resolves the card returns to its original location (unless otherwise affected).
atoms.notes: Reveal is a UI/procedural instruction, not an engine invariant. No skirmish-scope DC/CC uses reveal in a way that requires oracle-pinning.

atoms.summary: Each evade result removes one surge result at the end of the Apply Modifiers step, reducing the number of surges the attacker can spend.
atoms.notes: Evade-cancels-surge mechanic is pinned by the existing ATK-013 (Apply Modifiers) / ATK-014 (Spend Surges) step atoms.

atoms.summary: Each surge ability can be triggered only once per attack.

assertions: 001: Bossk → ["damage 2", "pierce 2"]
004a: Bossk spending both surges (damage 2 + pierce 2) → correct final damage

atoms.notes: Once-per-attack surge rule pinned by surge-legality-probes (surge list enumeration + dual-spend resolution confirms single-trigger per ability).

atoms.summary: During a campaign, a hero performing an attack may spend one surge to recover one strain (limit once per attack).
atoms.notes: Campaign-only surge-for-strain recovery (scope:definitional because scope enum excludes 'campaign'); skirmish has no heroes.

atoms.summary: A surge spent on a keyword ability (Blast, Cleave, condition keyword) adds the keyword during Spend Surges; the keyword's effect performs/applies after the attack resolves if the target suffered damage.
atoms.notes: Blast/Cleave timing already captured by BLST atoms and the after-attack-resolves step ATK-017.

atoms.summary: Time-period values restrict which Side Mission cards and Agenda sets may be included in a given campaign.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only army-building constraint (scope:definitional because scope enum excludes 'campaign'); no skirmish analog.

atoms.summary: All text on cards and hero sheets are called abilities; abilities can be mandatory or optional ("may", "use", or cost-to-activate makes them optional). If any part cannot be performed, the player performs as much as possible.
atoms.notes: Mandatory/optional taxonomy + "do-as-much-as-possible" rule. Enforced per-card; no generic oracle.

atoms.summary: An ability that is "used" can be triggered multiple times per round, but each ability can only be triggered once per timing instance (e.g., "Use while attacking" is once per attack).
atoms.notes: Once-per-timing-instance for abilities. SUR-002 pins the per-attack once-only for surge abilities; same contract extends to other timing instances by the same rule.

atoms.summary: Ability costs include special-action, surge, strain, threat, exhaust, deplete, discard/play, and VP.
atoms.notes: Taxonomy of ability costs. Surge-cost pinned by ATK-014 (Spend Surges); exhaust pinned by EXH; VP cost pinned by VPS-004. Strain and threat/deplete are downstream definitional.

atoms.summary: A figure can perform each special action ability only once per activation.
atoms.notes: Same rule as CRR-ACT-007 (one-per-activation special). Pinned by 'rejects duplicate special (specialsUsed)' + 'already been used' in tests/domain/oracle/dc-ability-behavioral.test.js.

atoms.summary: A "during your activation" ability can be used before or after an action within an activation; these are not interrupting abilities and cannot be used while resolving another ability.
atoms.notes: Between-actions ability surfacing. Implemented per-card; no isolated oracle.

atoms.summary: An ability that causes damage (such as Force Choke) is not considered an attack and does not count toward attack-per-activation limits.
atoms.notes: Same rule as CRR-ATK-039 (Force Choke is not an attack). Pinned by Phase-2 Force Choke probe in tests/domain/oracle/dc-ability-behavioral.test.js.

atoms.summary: Imperial Class "Attachment" cards are placed on Deployment cards when figures deploy; abilities apply to all figures in the group.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only Imperial Class attachment mechanic (scope:definitional because campaign-only). Skirmish has a separate SKIRMISH ATTACHMENTS section covered by SKA-*.

atoms.summary: When the last figure in a group is defeated, attached Imperial Class cards return to the player's play area and may be re-attached on future deployments.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only recycle flow for Imperial Class attachments. Not applicable in skirmish.

atoms.summary: Many attachments require the group to have a specific trait (e.g., TROOPER); attachments with trait restrictions cannot be played on groups lacking the trait.
atoms.notes: Trait restriction on Imperial Class attachments (campaign). Skirmish Upgrade attachments handle this via SKA atoms.

atoms.summary: Tokens are not limited; dice can be re-rolled as needed without counting as a reroll; cards that run out cannot be drawn or used further.
atoms.notes: Physical-component workarounds. Engine uses in-memory pools; no scarcity invariant to oracle.

atoms.summary: In a campaign, players are limited to the physical figures supplied; expansion packs define specific limits.
atoms.notes: Campaign figure-pool limits (scope:definitional because campaign-only).

atoms.summary: In a skirmish, a player can have at most: one of each unique Deployment card, two of each elite Deployment card, and four of each regular Deployment card.
atoms.notes: Army-composition copy limits. Enforced at army-build time in UI / /start flow; no dedicated oracle pins "copy-count cap" for uniques/elites/regulars.

atoms.summary: During a skirmish, outside of attacks, mission rules resolve first, then effects from the player with initiative, then each other player clockwise.
atoms.notes: Initiative-first ordering outside attacks is the core contract pinned by CNF-007 (sor-sequencing-probes).

atoms.summary: If multiple mission rules would resolve at the same time, the player with initiative decides their order.
atoms.notes: Mission-rule tie-break by initiative. CNF-008 already captures this branch.

atoms.summary: During setup of a skirmish, players place all of their figures within their deployment zone.
atoms.notes: Top-level pointer to the detailed "Deploy Units" step in Skirmish Mission Setup (SKMS-004).

atoms.summary: All non-hero figures have corresponding Deployment cards listing group name, size, abilities, Speed, Health, Defense, and attack.
atoms.notes: Data schema of DC records. Stored in data/dc-effects.json.

atoms.summary: A Deployment card with a Campaign Deployment Icon is campaign-only; a Skirmish Deployment Icon makes it skirmish-only.
atoms.notes: Play-mode restriction. Enforced by army-builder filter; no oracle needed.

atoms.summary: Elite Deployment cards have a red border; regular Deployment cards have gray borders.
atoms.notes: Visual taxonomy. Data-only distinction.

atoms.summary: Unique cards are identified by a bullet (▪) before the name (e.g., "▪ Darth Vader").
atoms.notes: Naming convention. Uniqueness enforcement is structural (see UNI-*).

atoms.summary: The SKIRMISH UPGRADE trait excludes cards from rules/abilities referencing Deployment cards unless explicitly stated (e.g., "Temporary Alliance" and "Take Initiative" exclusions).
atoms.notes: Skirmish Upgrade exclusion already pinned by CDC-004 (status-phase-behavioral 003c).

atoms.summary: Saska Teft uses device tokens to grant herself and fellow Rebels abilities; these tokens only interact with abilities on Saska's Hero sheet and Class cards.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only hero-specific token (Saska Teft). No skirmish presence.

atoms.summary: A Form card adds its text box and abilities box to a Deployment card; placed below the DC when gained; text is treated as though on the DC.
atoms.notes: Only Clawdite Shapeshifter uses Form cards in the current corpus. Form-swap mechanics are niche; no dedicated oracle.

atoms.summary: A Deployment card can only gain a Form card with a subname corresponding to that Deployment card's name.
atoms.notes: Subname-matching rule enforced by data; no runtime invariant worth oracle-pinning.

atoms.summary: Form Cards are unique: only 1 copy of each Form card can be in play at a time; in skirmish, only 1 copy per army.
atoms.notes: Form-card uniqueness (M28 in testing audit is the open gap for Clawdite form uniqueness — still OPEN per memory). Gap confirmed.

atoms.summary: A locked door cannot be opened until the mission rules unlock it.
atoms.notes: Delegates to the DOORS section (DOR-*), which already covers open/closed/locked door states.

atoms.summary: The map for each skirmish mission is shown in its diagram; rules for each skirmish mission are listed on Skirmish Mission cards.
atoms.notes: Data-definitional (mission cards). Missions are declared in data/missions/.

atoms.summary: Setup Step 1 — Bring Armies and Command Cards: both players place Deployment cards faceup in their play areas and shuffle their 15-card Command decks.
atoms.notes: Procedural setup. Bot hands players pre-built armies; CC shuffle happens at game-start.

atoms.summary: Setup Step 2 — Determine Initiative: the player with the lowest total Deployment-card cost chooses who begins with the initiative token (random on tie).
atoms.implementationArea: src/handlers/setup.js (handleInitiativeRoll: lower-cost squad wins, tie → random) + src/engine/setup-bridge.js (headless parity)

assertions: 002a: handler — Discord setup sums both squad costs before picking winner
002b: handler — lower-cost path assigns initiative to the cheaper squad
002c: handler — ties fall back to a 50/50 coin flip
002d: bridge — headless setup also uses lower-cost + random tiebreak
002e: behavior — pure predicate matches CRR semantics
handler must award initiative to the lower-cost player — CRR-SKMS-002
tied-cost fallback must be random — CRR-SKMS-002

atoms.summary: Setup Step 3 — Determine and Set Up Skirmish Mission: the initiative player draws a skirmish mission card; players build the map, place tokens, and observe the A/B letter selector.
atoms.notes: Physical map/token setup. Bot loads mission-specific configuration from data/missions/.

atoms.summary: Setup Step 4 — Deploy Units: the initiative player chooses a deployment zone and places all their figures there; opposing players then deploy, choosing from remaining zones.

assertions: 004a: source — zone-choice interaction is gated to the initiative player (or Devious Scheme override)
004b: source — the chosen zone is recorded on game.deploymentZoneChosen (single source of truth)
004c: source — the opposing player is assigned the complementary zone (red <-> blue)
004d: source — deploy-time zone lookup resolves each player to their assigned zone

atoms.summary: Setup Step 5 — Draw Command Cards: set the round dial to 1; each player draws 3 cards from their Command deck.
atoms.notes: Draw-3-at-setup pinned by CC-001 / CCD-001.

atoms.summary: A Skirmish Upgrade card with a negative deployment cost increases the total deployment budget of the rest of the army by its magnitude (e.g., -4 cost allows the remainder to total up to 44).
atoms.notes: Negative-cost budget math. Enforced at army-build time; no oracle pins the budget arithmetic.

atoms.summary: A negative-cost attachment requires at least one eligible Deployment card in the army; when a group with such an attachment is defeated, VPs scored are modified by the negative cost.
atoms.notes: Attachment-cost VP adjustment branch. WIN-005 / SKA-004 cover the (positive) attachment-cost side; negative-cost scoring is the symmetric case with sign flipped.

atoms.summary: No player controls a neutral figure; neutral figures cannot activate or perform actions.
atoms.notes: Neutral-figure activation exclusion. Rare in skirmish (mission-specific); no dedicated oracle.

atoms.summary: Neutral figures cannot suffer damage or be targeted by attacks, abilities, or game effects except as specified by mission rules.
atoms.notes: Neutral damage/target immunity. Mission-specific; no generic oracle.

atoms.summary: Figures can move through spaces containing neutral figures at no additional cost but cannot end movement there (unless companion or Massive).
atoms.notes: Neutral-space movement allowance. Mission-specific; no generic oracle.

atoms.summary: Neutral figures block line of sight.
atoms.notes: Neutral LOS block. Mission-specific; no generic oracle.

atoms.summary: In a campaign, optional deployments allow the Imperial player to spend threat to deploy groups and/or reinforce figures; the Deploy and Reinforce step of the Status Phase is an optional deployment.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only (scope:definitional); no skirmish analog (skirmish uses open-group reinforce).

atoms.summary: During a campaign, a hero can perform a rest action to recover strain equal to Endurance (and convert overflow into damage recovery).
atoms.notes: Campaign-only rest mechanic (hero figures do not exist in skirmish).

atoms.summary: A figure adjacent to or in the same space as a token can perform an interact action to retrieve the token; the token then moves with the figure.

assertions: 003: Bossk (normal) at terminal h21 → interact offered
005: P1 Stormtrooper (cost 6) at terminal, P2 Obi-Wan 3 spaces away → no interact

atoms.notes: Interact-to-retrieve is the generic token-claim mechanism. Pinned by interact-legality-probes 003 (offered when adjacent) and 005 (Alter Mind exclusion).

atoms.summary: A carried token cannot be retrieved by others or dropped voluntarily; on figure defeat, carried tokens drop in the figure's space.
atoms.notes: Token-drop-on-defeat. Mission-specific (e.g., capture-the-flag variants); no dedicated oracle.

atoms.summary: Retrieving a token is not claiming a token.
atoms.notes: Terminology distinction. Handled per-mission; retrieve = pickup, claim = permanent acquisition (CLM-*).

atoms.summary: Each round of a skirmish consists of an Activation Phase followed by a Status Phase.
atoms.notes: Round structure. Activation Phase section already covered by APH atoms.

atoms.summary: Starting with the initiative player, players take turns activating groups; a player with fewer ready DCs than any opponent can pass instead of activating.
atoms.notes: Alternation + pass-when-fewer-ready-DCs is the ACV-002 (activation alternation) + ACV-007 (exhausted player skipped) contract.

atoms.summary: The player with initiative breaks all ties for mission rules (e.g., equidistant figures).
atoms.notes: Initiative tiebreak. CFS-002 and CNF-008 already pin this.

atoms.summary: When mission rules instruct to randomly place tokens, the Imperial player shuffles the tokens facedown at indicated spaces; no player may examine the facedown side until revealed.
atoms.notes: Random-facedown token placement. Mission-specific (Sabacc, crate-reveal missions); no dedicated oracle pins the "facedown-hidden" invariant.

atoms.summary: When mission rules instruct to choose and place tokens, the Imperial player places them facedown in chosen indicated spaces; Rebel players cannot examine them; once placed they cannot be moved, but Imperial can examine them.
atoms.notes: Imperial-choose placement variant. Similar to SSU-001 but Imperial keeps knowledge. No oracle.

atoms.summary: In a skirmish, when a figure suffers strain, it suffers equal damage instead; the controlling player can prevent that damage by discarding one Command card from the top of their deck per point of prevention.

assertions: B-C-PEND-001: handleStrainChoice alldmg clears pendingStrainChoice
B-C-PEND-002: handleStrainChoice discard path clears pendingStrainChoice
B-C-STRAIN-001: alldmg path applies full HP damage

atoms.notes: Strain-as-damage + CC-discard-to-prevent pinned by combat-behavioral B-C-PEND-001/002 and B-C-STRAIN-001.

atoms.summary: Tress Hacnua uses style tokens to enhance her melee attacks and build to finishing strikes; these tokens only interact with abilities on Tress's Hero sheet and Class cards.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only hero-specific token (Tress Hacnua). No skirmish presence.

atoms.summary: Tests redirects to Attribute Tests.
atoms.notes: Pure-pointer section. Attribute Tests (ATT-*) already covers the semantics.

atoms.summary: During a campaign, a wounded hero who is defeated withdraws: removed from the map, cannot be activated, abilities unavailable, can still help with group decisions.
atoms.notes: Campaign-only wounded-hero withdrawal. Skirmish has no heroes and no wounded state.
